title: Fix transposed sample.int() arguments in plot_rope_probs()
description:
`plot_rope_probs()` called `sample.int(1, 1000)` for the contrast seed, which swaps the arguments of `sample.int(n, size)`. Evaluating that call errors (`cannot take a sample larger than the population`). It never surfaces today because `rstanarm::posterior_epred()` ignores `seed`, so the promise is never forced. This changes it to `sample.int(10000, 1)`, matching the rest of the package.

Plot output is unchanged: the ROPE probabilities are identical before and after.

The new test mocks `contrast_models()` to force and capture the seed. It fails on the old code with the `sample.int()` error and passes now.

Closes #82

title: added tools for comparing to the current best model
description:
Adds `compare_to_leader()` and an `autoplot()` methods. There is also a new `select_best` option for `perf_mod()`. 

Example: 

``` r
library(tidymodels)
#> Warning: package 'dials' was built under R version 4.6.1
#> Warning: package 'modeldata' was built under R version 4.6.1
library(tidyposterior)

ames_log <-
  ames |>
  mutate(Sale_Price  = log10(Sale_Price)) |>
  select(Sale_Price, Latitude, Longitude, Neighborhood, Gr_Liv_Area)

set.seed(4595)
data_split <- initial_split(ames_log, strata = "Sale_Price")
ames_train <- training(data_split)
ames_test  <- testing(data_split)
rs <- vfold_cv(ames_train)
```

``` r
# Tune or resample some models

ctrl_grid <- control_grid(save_workflow = TRUE)
ctrl_rs <- control_resamples(save_workflow = TRUE)

basic_rec <-
  recipe(Sale_Price ~ ., data = ames_train)

spline_rec <-
  basic_rec |>
  step_spline_natural(Latitude, Longitude, deg_free = 10)

set.seed(102)
linear_res <-
  workflow_set(
    preproc = list(basic = basic_rec, splines = spline_rec),
    models = list(linear_reg = linear_reg())
  ) |>
  workflow_map(
    fn = "fit_resamples",
    resamples = rs,
    control = ctrl_rs
  )
#> → A | error:   factor Neighborhood has new levels Landmark
#> There were issues with some computations   A: x1
#> → B | error:   factor Neighborhood has new levels Green_Hills
#> There were issues with some computations   A: x1There were issues with some computations   A: x1   B: x1
#> 
#> → A | error:   factor Neighborhood has new levels Landmark
#> → B | error:   factor Neighborhood has new levels Green_Hills

set.seed(102)
cart_res <-
  decision_tree(
    mode = "regression",
    cost_complexity = tune(),
    min_n = tune()
  ) |>
  tune_grid(
    Sale_Price ~ .,
    resamples = rs,
    grid = 25,
    control = ctrl_grid
  )


set.seed(102)
mars_res <-
  mars(
    mode = "regression",
    num_terms = tune(),
    prod_degree = tune()
  ) |>
  tune_grid(
    Sale_Price ~ .,
    resamples = rs,
    grid = 25,
    control = ctrl_grid
  )
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'plotrix'
#> 
#> The following object is masked from 'package:scales':
#> 
#>     rescale

model_set <-
  as_workflow_set(CART = cart_res, MARS = mars_res) |>
  bind_rows(linear_res)
```

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to tidyposterior website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the tidyposterior website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

title: Don't import pretty methods
description:
In https://github.com/tidymodels/rsample/pull/303, we're looking to not explicitly export the `pretty` S3 methods for rset objects. These are imported by `tidyposterior`, but removing them doesn't appear to have any negative effects. This PR removes them so we can remove them from rsample.

Note that R CMD check fails because of gtools, unrelated to the changes in this PR.
